'''Wei Biao Wu''' is a Chinese-born statistician.  He is a professor of [[statistics]] at the University of Chicago.

==Education and career==
Wu attended [[Fudan University]], receiving his bachelor's degree in 1997.{{cn|date=October 2023}} He went on to the [[University of Michigan]] for graduate studies, receiving his PhD in 2001 under the supervision of [[Michael Woodroofe]] and [[Sándor Csörgő]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=133376|title=Wei Biao Wu}}</ref>  He was hired at the [[University of Chicago]] shortly after completing his PhD, and has remained there since.

Wu is best-known for his work on [[Weakly dependent random variables|dependence]], in which the main new idea is to interpret random processes as physical systems, and to examine coefficients that would have physical meaning.<ref name="weakdep">{{cite book | last1=Dedecker | first1=Jérôme|last2=Doukhan|first2=Paul|last3=Lang|first3=Gabriel|last4=León R.|first4=José Rafael|last5=Louhichi|first5=Sana|last6=Prieur|first6=Clémentine | title=Weak dependence : with examples and applications | publisher=Springer | location=New York | year=2007 | isbn=978-0-387-69951-6 | oclc=191465311 | page=32|mr=2338725}}</ref><ref name="Wu2005">{{cite journal|last1=Wu|first1=W. B.|title=Nonlinear system theory: Another look at dependence|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=102|issue=40|year=2005|pages=14150–14154|issn=0027-8424|doi=10.1073/pnas.0506715102|pmid=16179388|pmc=1242319|bibcode=2005PNAS..10214150W|mr=2172215|doi-access=free}}</ref>  According to [[Google Scholar]], this work has been cited over 350 times.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?cites=1217648600425911396|title=Google Scholar citations for "Nonlinear systems theory: another look at dependence"|access-date=September 23, 2019}}</ref>  Wu has written over 100 papers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stat.uchicago.edu/~wbwu/papers.html|title=Wei Biao Wu's publication list|access-date=September 23, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/search/author.html?mrauthid=652125 |title=Wei Biao Wu author profile|website=[[MathSciNet]]|publisher=American Mathematical Society|url-access=subscription}}
</ref>

Wu has more than 20 students and their descendants working in academia.

== Most-cited publications ==
* His most cited article, WB Wu, Nonlinear system theory: Another look at dependence in ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]]'' (2005) 2005 Oct 4;102(40):14150-4. [https://scholar.google.com/scholar?output=instlink&q=info:ZFSjYfP05RAJ:scholar.google.com/&hl=en&as_sdt=0,33&scillfp=11337873248516776815&oi=lle] (open access) has been cited 485 times, according to Google Scholar.<ref name="GS">[https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C33&sciodt=0%2C33&cites=1217648600425911396&scipsc=&q=Wei+Biao+Wu&btnG= Google Scholar Author page], Accessed December 31, 2021</ref>
*Wu WB, Pourahmadi M. Nonparametric estimation of large covariance matrices of longitudinal data. ''[[Biometrika]]''. 2003 Dec 1;90(4):831-44. [http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.417.8377&rep=rep1&type=pdf] (open access) has been cited 341 times, according to Google Scholar <ref name=GS />
*Wu WB. Strong invariance principles for dependent random variables. The ''[[Annals of Probability]]''. 2007;35(6):2294-320. [https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-probability/volume-35/issue-6/Strong-invariance-principles-for-dependent-random-variables/10.1214/009117907000000060.pdf] (open access)  has been cited 235  times, according to Google Scholar  <ref name="GS" />
*Wu WB, Shao X. Limit theorems for iterated random functions. ''[[Journal of Applied Probability]]''. 2004 Jun;41(2):425-36. [http://www.stat.uchicago.edu/~wbwu/papers/1082999076.pdf] has been cited  194 times, according to Google Scholar <ref name="GS" />
*Wu WB, Zhao Z. Inference of trends in time series. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (Statistical Methodology). 2007 Jun;69(3):391-410. [https://rss.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1111/j.1467-9868.2007.00594.x] (open access) (Cited 172 times, according to Google Scholar.<ref name=GS  />)  
*Shao X, Wu WB. Asymptotic spectral theory for nonlinear time series. ''[[The Annals of Statistics]]''. 2007 Aug;35(4):1773-801. [](open access) (Cited 199 times, according to Google Scholar. [https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-statistics/volume-35/issue-4/Asymptotic-spectral-theory-for-nonlinear-time-series/10.1214/009053606000001479.pdf] (open access) <ref name=GS  />)  
 
In all, he has published 38 papers with ≥38 citations each.<ref name=GS  />

==Personal life==
Wu has practiced [[Falun Gong]] since 1998. His religious practices and criticism of the [[Chinese Communist Party]] led to inaction on his 2005 request for renewal of his [[Chinese passport]]. Following the loss of his Chinese passport, Wu's [[Chinese nationality law|Chinese nationality]] was also revoked.<ref>{{cite news |title=University of Chicago professor rejected for Chinese passport renewal because he practices Falun Gong |url=http://en.minghui.org/html/articles/2006/12/20/81021.html |accessdate=15 October 2019 |publisher=Minghui.org |date=20 December 2006 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120531020218/http://en.minghui.org/html/articles/2006/12/20/81021.html |archivedate=31 May 2012}} [http://www.clearharmony.net/articles/a37077-University-of-Chicago-Professor-Rejected-for-Chinese-Passport-Renewal-Because-He-Practises-Falun-Gong.html Alt URL]</ref>
